Create docs/design/proposal/architecture/accounting-records-contract-v1.md as a supplement to the preserved accounting and replay contracts. Define field-level types, required/optional/null rules, enums, ownership and digest references for EconomicEvent/request, TreatmentAssessment, JournalProposal, committed StateTransitionReceipt and response/rejection envelopes. Cover entity/book/branch identity, event version, opening state, context, economic/reporting time, evidence admission, authority/method/assumption versions and lineage. Every dependency must resolve to a typed record; distinguish absent information from explicit unknowns. Define the journal account/concept mapping, dimensions, currency/unit/scale, basis, amount/sign and rounding rules needed by this finite profile. Save this completed section before preparing examples.

Specify each outcome without conflating receipt validity, treatment eligibility, computation and commitment. A committed receipt references the original request, assessment, journal, delta and opening/closing states. Replay returns that immutable receipt with separate response metadata. Pre-evaluation rejection preserves submitted content and reasons without inventing a valid canonical request fingerprint. Unresolved or ineligible treatment produces no committed journal/delta. Reuse the existing common status vocabulary, including mathematical_status=unresolved and computation_status=not_computed for pre-evaluation rejection; keep accounting validity and human acceptance separate. Explicitly distinguish diagnostic candidate journals from committed journals.

Define the atomic boundary over identity index, journal, selected closing state and committed receipt. A confirmed validation failure or aborted commit leaves all four unchanged; optional rejection audit storage is separate. Recheck identity absence and opening-state freshness at commitment. Specify lost acknowledgement as unknown commit status until authoritative receipt lookup resolves it, never as a confirmed rollback or permission to post under a new identity. Describe complete before/after outcomes and retry obligations as design requirements; defer database isolation, crash-recovery algorithms and enforcement to persistence work.
